prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- There’s no single official service that can tell you “ChatGPT recommends X” because most LLMs don’t expose their training corpus or live source list.  
- For practical monitoring and to maximize the chance AI assistants will recommend your business, use a local-SEO / citation-monitoring service (my top pick: BrightLocal) plus manual testing against major chat assistants (Bing Chat, Perplexity, ChatGPT with browsing/Bing enabled, Google Assistant).

Why BrightLocal (or similar) is best in practice
- AI assistants that recommend local businesses usually pull from the same places customers and search engines use: Google Business Profile, Bing/Apple Maps, Yelp, TripAdvisor, big directories, and authoritative websites.  
- BrightLocal (and competitors Moz Local, Whitespark) give a consolidated view: citation accuracy across directories, local rank tracking (local pack), review monitoring, Google Business Profile health, and alerts. That’s the most direct way to see whether you’re visible in the sources assistants use.

How to check if AI is recommending you (practical steps)
1. Claim and optimize core profiles immediately: Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, Facebook/Meta, TripAdvisor. Make NAP (name/address/phone) consistent and add LocalBusiness schema on your site.  
2. Use a local-SEO service:
   - BrightLocal (recommended) — citation audit, rank tracking, review monitoring, local-pack testing.
   - Alternatives: Moz Local, Whitespark, SEMrush (local toolkit).  
3. Monitor web presence:
   - Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools (indexing, search traffic).  
   - Google Alerts, Mention, Brand24 for web mentions.  
4. Manually test AI assistants:
   - Ask Bing Chat, Perplexity, Claude, Bard, and ChatGPT (with web access) targeted prompts like “Recommend a [service] near [city/zip]” and request sources/citations. Record whether your business appears and what sources are cited. Bing Chat and Perplexity are especially useful because they cite URLs.  
5. Improve signals that make AIs cite you:
   - High-quality local landing pages, structured data (LocalBusiness schema), consistent citations, lots of genuine reviews (Google/Yelp), and strong backlinks from relevant sites.  
6. Track results and iterate: use BrightLocal/Moz to watch changes in citation accuracy, local rankings, and review volume; retest assistants after changes.

When to use specialized services
- Reputation management at scale: Reputation.com.  
- Enterprise/large multi-location brands: local-SEO tools from SEMrush or Whitespark plus custom monitoring.  
- If you just want free/basic checks: claim Google Business Profile and run manual queries against Bing Chat/Perplexity and set Google Alerts.

Bottom line
- Best single service to “check” visibility for AI-based recommendations: BrightLocal (or Moz Local/Whitespark if you prefer).  
- Complement it by claiming major profiles and manually querying AI chat services (Bing Chat, Perplexity, ChatGPT with web access) to see if you’re actually being recommended and cited.
